text.p: Italian debt markets shed their gains by the close of trade while the lira was trading on the weak side of the 1,000 per mark barrier.

Dealers said the market had performed well in the course of the day on lower than expected preliminary inflation rates for March. Data from seven sample cities showed month on month CPI at 0.1 percent and year on year inflation at 2.2 percent.
If confirmed by the last four sample cities releasing their data after 1630 GMT, the rate will be slightly lower than the 2.3 percent forecast by analysts and February's 2.4 year on year rate.

The November 2006 Btp ended nine bps up at 100.89, yielding 7.77 percent and with a spread over the 10-year benchmark Bund of 185 basis points. The most traded July 2006 Btp was 24 basis points higher at 105.99. The July LIFFE future was three basis points lower at 125.08.
A summary of Italy's quarterly accounts said any further interest rate cuts would be modest. The summary also said Italian GDP would not grow by more than 1.2 percent in 1997.
Italy requires 15-16 trillion lire of deficit cutting measures in its proposed mini-budget, cabinet secretary Enrico Micheli said.
But Micheli said all options on the content of the mini-budget were still open.
